- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–10 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average within 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates in early days (1–7) when sentiment is neutral or bearish; increase forecast by 3–7% for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or negative), model tends to lag; add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–10 days to catch momentum.
